title: San Jacinto Club and keno games
summary: Dejan belonged only to his father's San Jacinto Club, remembers its matinees, boxing and keno, and playing with Manuel Perez.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you belong to any clubs ever?
No, no I didn't belong to any one of the clubs.

I know in general sometimes the Catholic Church doesn't approve of belonging to some other Lodges of course like Masons I think but is there any rule that you couldn't have belonged to any of those clubs? No, no.

But I belonged to one of the one club I belonged to was the San Jacinto's. Oh yes. See my father belonged to them and he made my brother and I a member of the club. That's the only club I ever belonged to. Is that still running?
I know the hall is. Yeah.
No, no, no, no, no, no they don't have, I don't think they have no club. The hall is running, you know, for dance and so forth and so on.
Somebody said, I was talking to somebody the other day, they say Binzie I think owns that, doesn't he? Or his brother or something? I don't know, I mean, he might.

He might just own this. But I don't know, I mean, the club never should let it get away from him, you know. They had a nice club one time. Every Sunday evening they had matinee and boxing, you know, and they had card games and, yeah. They had a good time.

They had to just have a keno game a while before they should stop it. I don't know why, what reason they would stop a keno game or a bingo game and let racehorses go out, I don't know why. Never to try to seek and find out why, but you could play a card for a nickel, you go to the track you gotta pay at least two dollars to bet on the horse. People used to come home on a Saturday night with their bag of groceries, with their basket of groceries under their arm that they won at the keno game, you know, and this one coming with their ham in their arm. Yeah, sometimes they had their whole Sunday dinner in a basket. I remember playing with Manny Perez a couple of times after he started to renew a band just like Piran did, you know, changed his band.
